title: Six narratives about the true value of open repositories
content:
For too long, repositories have been described as background utilities: useful, worthy, and easy to overlook. That framing no longer fits. Scholarly communication is being reshaped by geopolitical pressures, integrity scandals, AI, and a long-overdue rethink of how research is assessed. In each case, repositories turn out to be important aspects of the solution. COAR’s New Narratives Series for Repositories sets out that case in six areas:

1. The public value of repositories

After decades of sustained investment, there are now thousands of open access repositories worldwide collecting and preserving research outputs. Open by design and containing hundreds of millions of research products, repositories give humans and machines barrier-free access to research, and together they form a key pillar of global research infrastructure. Open access repositories have long been recognised as essential infrastructure for the
research community, but their value extends far beyond the academy. Repositories serve diverse publics, from physicians and educators to entrepreneurs and community organisers around the world, providing access to knowledge that would otherwise remain locked behind paywalls.
